Karoly Poka and Adam Young research Egypt's monuments with instruments and patience. They join Danny Jones to argue that new scans reveal ancient Egyptian machines. In their reading, the devices and engineering prove the human timeline wrong. They push advanced capability far earlier than the standard chronology allows.

The guests explain their scan work and the features they believe no hand tool explains. Jones works through the strongest examples and the objections Egyptology raises. Their conclusions are their own, outside the field's consensus, and the episode keeps them labeled by its own framing. Listeners get the current, measurement-based form of an old argument: that the oldest stones were cut by a technology the record lost. The scans can be argued over; the stones, as the guests note, are patient.

Comedian Bassem Youssef joins Danny Jones to give what he calls the real reason Benjamin Netanyahu visits the White House so often. Youssef is an Egyptian comic known for sharp satire of power. He brings jokes and a hard edge.

Youssef reads the visits as a sign of who needs whom in the US and Israel bond. He roasts both sides with the eye of a man raised under strongmen. Jones lets the jokes land, then asks for the real claim. Listeners get satire with a thesis. The library holds the talk as an archive record of his stated view.
